prompt: Carreto's wiki page had 61 rules. Renata deleted 38 and turned 14 into guidelines. How many remained standards?
Put the steps Carreto took to retire the carreto-http rule in order.
items: Announce a date and what replaces the rule
Remove the check on that date
Mark the ADR that introduced it as superseded

prompt: A rule belongs among the standards only if a machine or a reviewer can answer it with yes or ___.
hint: Lesson 9, the test that sorts a standard from a guideline.

prompt: A company publishes a new standard: "Services must be resilient." Applying the lesson's test, what is it?
hint: Lesson 9: can anybody answer yes or no?

choices.text: A strong standard, because it is written with must
choices.why: The word must does not make a rule checkable; two reviewers would disagree on what resilient means.

choices.text: A direction at best, until it is rewritten as a rule with a yes-or-no answer
choices.why: Right: rewritten as, say, a time limit for recovery or a retry rule, it becomes a candidate standard.

choices.text: A guideline, because it uses no numbers
choices.why: Numbers help, but the test is whether a yes or no answer exists.

choices.text: A fitness function, because it is about an architectural characteristic
choices.why: A fitness function is an automated check; this is a sentence nobody can run.

prompt: A team turns on a new dependency check over a codebase that already has 40 violations. Which start does the lesson recommend?

choices.text: Fail the build from the first run, so that the 40 are fixed quickly
choices.why: That blocks every team for code most of them did not write, and the check gets switched off.

choices.text: Leave it in report-only mode until the 40 are gone
choices.why: Then new violations keep arriving while the old ones are fixed.

choices.text: Freeze the 40 in a baseline and fail only on new ones
choices.why: Right: the baseline only shrinks, so the code reaches the rule without a week of blocked merges.

choices.text: Fix the 40 first, then write the check
choices.why: Months without a check means new violations arrive faster than old ones leave.

prompt: An exception request answers "until when?" with "when the other team has time". What should the owner of the standard do?
hint: Lesson 9, the three questions before granting.

choices.text: Grant it and renew it later if needed
choices.why: An exception with no real date has nothing for the build to expire on.

choices.text: Ask for a date tied to planned work
choices.why: Right: a date anchored to work already planned is a real one; a wish is not.

choices.text: Refuse it and remove the standard
choices.why: One vague request says nothing about the standard.

choices.text: Grant it without a date, since dates only create pressure
choices.why: Without a date the exception becomes a second, unwritten standard.
